$doc: THE SFX CATALOG (Mike, 2026-10-20: 'a library.json in the SFX folder like the music one, telling us when something should be used'). Two parts. `loose` = the sound files that sit in this root folder (hand-edited here, because comps and scripts reference them by this path). `index` = GENERATED, one row per sound across EVERY subfolder library (Impacts/, risers/, accents/, braams/, drones/, downshifters/, ding/, kinetic-text/) plus `loose`, so a picker reads ONE file and never listens. Rebuild with `python video-creation/skills/sfx-library/scripts/sfx_catalog.py build`; `check` lists any file on disk that no library describes (an orphan is a rule violation: every new SFX gets a library row the day it lands). Skill: video-creation/skills/sfx-library/sfx-library.md.
$schema_note: Pick fields, the same on every row: `type` (impact / riser / whoosh / accent / braam / drone / downshifter / ding / stinger / kinetic-text / reaction), `mood_class` (dark / tense / epic / hype / neutral, the HARD-GATE mood of longform-edited.md section 7), `character` (what it sounds like), `trigger` (the on-screen EVENT it is cut to), `best_for` (when to reach for it over its neighbours). Measured fields: `duration_sec`, `attack_sec` (seconds from file start to the loudest sample: place the file so the attack lands ON the event's frame), `peak_dbfs`, `tail_sec` (how long it rings after the peak, 30 dB down; a long tail smears over the next cut). `used_in[]` is frozen history; live usage is the graph's usage ledger (video-creation/assets/usage-ledger.json).
